newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran's might no threat to others - guards chief.
newsitem.headline: Iran's might no threat to others - guards chief.

text.p: Iran's military might is no threat to other countries as long as the Islamic republic is not threatened, the commander-in-chief of the Iranian revolutionary guards said on Sunday ahead of wargames in the Gulf.

Major General Mohsen Rezaie, speaking to Iran's official news agency IRNA in the Gulf port of Bandar Abbas, said the Islamic revolution had always conveyed the message of peace and friendship to the world.

He said the objective of the impending amphibious exercise, code-named "Tarqi Qods" (Road to Jerusalem), was to upgrade the combat power of the Iranian armed forces in defending the power and glory of Islam in Iran.

The agency quoted Rezaei as saying the only way to counter the hegemony of global arrogance -- a term used in Iran to describe the United States -- was to attain self-sufficiency and to forge stronger unity among Moslems in all cultural, political, economic and military fields.
He stressed that the might of the Islamic Republic system did not pose a danger to the interests of other countries as long as Iran was not threatened.

Rezaei added that the enemies of revolution, in order to justify their presence in the region and continue with the plunder of the wealth of Gulf countries, had always portrayed Iran's military power as a threat to regional countries, IRNA said.

He reiterated statements by Iranian leaders that the Islamic Republic's military forces were ready to cooperate with regional countries in order to set up a "regional security and defence cooperation system" with no reliance on foreign forces.
IRNA earlier quoted the Commander of Regional Resistance, Brigadier General Abbas Alavi Nejad, as saying 50 battalions of guards would take part in the wargames.
Iran said on Tuesday its army would hold amphibious wargames in the Gulf this week to train for surprise attacks against "enemies" posing threats to the Islamic Republic.
Rezaei was quoted as saying 200,000 troops and volunteer Bassij forces would take part.
Iran regularly holds wargames in the Gulf.
